split_protocol: earliest 80% of traces by start time for training; latest 20% for test

features.name: agent_latency_zscore
features.contextual_rationale: A 500ms call is normal for a slow agent but anomalous for a fast agent; global thresholds would misclassify.

features.name: agent_retry_zscore
features.contextual_rationale: Retry behavior varies by agent configuration; absolute retry thresholds ignore agent-specific baselines.

features.name: agent_token_zscore
features.contextual_rationale: Token consumption depends on agent prompt templates and tool chains; only the agent's own history sets context.

features.name: agent_cost_zscore
features.contextual_rationale: Cost baselines must be agent-relative because different agents use different models and tools.

features.name: task_latency_zscore
features.contextual_rationale: A 100-tool-call trace is normal for order_lookup but abnormal for delivery_status; task context sets the norm.

features.name: task_retry_zscore
features.contextual_rationale: Retry storms are expected for complex multi-step tasks; task-relative z-scores distinguish normal complexity from failure.

features.name: task_token_zscore
features.contextual_rationale: Token budgets differ by task complexity; a high token count for a simple lookup is more suspicious than for a multi-step task.

features.name: task_cost_zscore
features.contextual_rationale: Cost spikes must be evaluated against the task's normal budget, not a global average.

features.name: agent_task_latency_zscore
features.contextual_rationale: Combines agent and task context: the same latency can be normal for agent A on task X but anomalous for agent B on task X.

features.name: agent_task_retry_zscore
features.contextual_rationale: Retry behavior is most comparable when both agent and task are held constant.

features.name: agent_task_token_zscore
features.contextual_rationale: Token usage varies by agent model and task complexity; the joint baseline is the fairest comparator.

features.name: agent_task_cost_zscore
features.contextual_rationale: Cost anomalies are most meaningful when compared to the specific agent-task pair's history.

features.name: call_position
features.derivation: 1-based index of this event within its trace's event sequence
features.contextual_rationale: Position matters because early vs late failures have different diagnostic meaning.

features.name: calls_so_far
features.derivation: Cumulative count of events in the trace up to and including this event
features.contextual_rationale: The same tool call count is normal for long workflows but abnormal for short ones; position provides that context.

features.name: time_since_last_call_ms
features.derivation: Milliseconds between this event and the previous event in the same trace; NaN for the first event
features.contextual_rationale: Inter-call timing reveals stalls and loops that absolute latency masks.

features.name: tool_repeat_in_session
features.derivation: Number of times the same tool_name has been called earlier in this trace (0 for first occurrence)
features.contextual_rationale: Repetition within a session signals loops or retries that a simple call count cannot distinguish.

features.name: permission_match
features.derivation: True if the event's declared permissions superset the tool's required permissions; False otherwise
features.contextual_rationale: Permission mismatches are policy violations, not statistical anomalies; this flag feeds both rules and risk engines.

features.name: trace_event_count
features.derivation: Total number of events in the trace (repeated for each event in the trace)
features.contextual_rationale: A 5-call trace is normal for simple tasks; without trace context, raw counts are meaningless.
